data.body:
[P2] Prevent cyclic waits between reentrant end hooks

Two branches can claim the end hooks of two completed callbacks concurrently. If each hook reads the other callback through `Callback.result()`, both reach this branch and wait on the other hook's completion event. Those events are set only after the hooks return, so the invocation deadlocks, including branch-pool shutdown. The owner check prevents self-waits but does not prevent this cross-thread cycle; these reads returned immediately before this change. Track active end-hook dispatch and make result reads within it inspection-only, while retaining ownership waits for ordinary result consumers. Add a regression test with two concurrently running hooks reading each other's already-terminal callback results.
